add-text-to-each-line.formula:
For every line L in your text:
output line = prefix + L + suffix

Example: prefix '- ', suffix '!', line 'apple' -> '- apple!'
With 'Skip empty lines' switched on, blank lines pass through unchanged.
howTo: Paste or type your text into the input box, one item per line.
Type the text to add before each line in the Prefix box (for example '- ' or '> ').
Type the text to add after each line in the Suffix box (for example ',' or '!'). Leave either box empty if you only need one side.
Keep 'Skip empty lines' on if you want blank lines left alone.
Copy the finished text or download it as a .txt file.

mistakes: Leaving 'Skip empty lines' off means blank lines get a stray prefix or suffix — your list suddenly has junk entries in the middle.
Adding a comma before each line does not make valid CSV — fields that already contain commas still need quoting.
Expecting the tool to number your lines (1., 2., 3.) — it only repeats the same text, so do the numbering in your spreadsheet first.
Typing a suffix with a trailing space adds invisible whitespace to every line, which breaks exact-match lookups later.
Pasting from a spreadsheet copies hidden tabs and extra spaces — clean the source first or the affix lands in the wrong place.
